question: Do barbless hooks really increase your catch rate?
answer: Yes — barbless hooks penetrate faster with less effort than barbed hooks because the point is not fighting against a barb to drive home. Think of it as the difference between a spear and a wedge. The masses of fly fishers believe a barbed hook keeps fish on better — but a better hookset technique is what actually keeps fish on, not the barb.

question: Do fish come off more easily on barbless hooks?
answer: Fish come off barbless hooks when the angler creates slack — not because of the hook design. Maintain a tight line and proper rod angle and the fish stays on. As a guide, Mac Brown finds it much easier to simply give a bit of slack and have the barbless hook fall out cleanly at the net — leading to faster releases and more fish landed throughout the day with far less handling.

question: What are the best barbless hooks for fly tying?
answer: Hanak, Fulling Mill, Dohiku, and Maturo produce excellent quality barbless wire that was not available to fly tiers years ago. These hooks ride inverted — hook up — and consistently take fish in the upper part of the mouth for a solid hook set. The quality of wire in modern barbless hooks is significantly better than older barbed hooks from traditional manufacturers.

question: Are barbless hooks required in Great Smoky Mountains National Park?
answer: Yes — artificial lures with single barbless hooks are required in Great Smoky Mountains National Park. The park's wild trout water is catch and release only with artificial flies and lures. Barbless hooks are not just an ethical choice on this water — they are the law.

question: How do I make a barbed hook barbless?
answer: Use hemostats or pliers to flatten the barb down toward the hook point — you do not need to remove it entirely, just get it flat enough that it no longer grips. Japanese chemically sharpened hooks with micro barbs are the easiest to crimp. Work slowly from the rear of the barb forward. Test with your thumbnail — if it catches, keep crimping.
